detail.longDescription: I paid $19 for Kimi Code to test K3.1 Pro Standard (not Highspeed) using the official CLI v2.3.1. I ran two tasks on small repositories: 1. Recommend movies based on an existing movie database. 2. Analyze a website's codebase. Neither task completed. The entire 5-hour quota was exhausted within minutes. I analyzed the actual session logs, including background agents: - Fresh input: 368,203 tokens - Cached input: 1,183,744 tokens - Output: 39,324 tokens - Total: 1.59M tokens At Kimi's published API rates, that's just $1.37 worth of usage before hitting the 5-hour limit which is easily less than 5% of what Claude Code offers at $20 subscription. The logs show: "429 You've reached your 5-hour usage limit." For comparison, Claude Code on a $20 subscription processed roughly 381M tokens over 4-5 hours using Opus 5.5 xhigh, mostly cached input. That's not a controlled benchmark, but the difference in usable capacity is staggering. Both Kimi tasks failed without delivering results. I have video evidence and detailed logs, but won't publish private repository data. Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hSr-DLn88AM Is this a quota-accounting bug, or are Kimi's $19 subscription limits intentionally this restrictive? Disclosure: I also develop a competing coding agent. These tests used Kimi's official CLI.
